item.title: 2 children removed from Lautoka home following alleged abuse and neglect
item.description: Two children who were allegedly victims of abuse and neglect have been removed from their house at Sukanaivalu Road in Lautoka and placed in the care of a relative. Police say they and Social Welfare officers in Lautoka attended to a report last night where it was alleged that two children were victims of abuse and neglect.
item.content:encoded:
Two children who were allegedly victims of abuse and neglect have been removed from their house at Sukanaivalu Road in Lautoka and placed in the care of a relative.

Police say they and Social Welfare officers in Lautoka attended to a report last night where it was alleged that two children were victims of abuse and neglect.

They say despite the efforts of officials, the children’s mother did not want to leave with the children.

Police are reminding everyone that under the Child Care and Protection Act 2024, failure to report suspected child abuse is an offence.

Members of the public are also urged to report issues against Police service delivery to 1681, or send them a message, photos or videos via WhatsApp, Viber and Signal on 9905922.

item.title: Fiji Airways reinstates direct Nadi-Nouméa flights
item.description: Fiji Airways has reinstated direct flights between Nadi and Nouméa, New Caledonia, to strengthen connectivity across the Pacific. The airline says the Nadi-Nouméa service will operate twice a week on Tuesdays and Fridays, adding more than 10,000 seats annually between Fiji and New Caledonia.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Airways has reinstated direct flights between Nadi and Nouméa, New Caledonia, to strengthen connectivity across the Pacific.

The airline says the Nadi-Nouméa service will operate twice a week on Tuesdays and Fridays, adding more than 10,000 seats annually between Fiji and New Caledonia.

Fiji Airways Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Paul Scurrah says the return of the service is an important milestone for the airline and the wider Pacific region which reinforces Fiji's position as a connecting hub for the Pacific .

Scurrah says travellers from New Caledonia will also be able to connect through Nadi to Fiji Airways' wider network across the Pacific, New Zealand, Asia, Australia and North America.

He says the service will make it easier for people to travel between Fiji and New Caledonia for holidays, business and to visit family.

He says Nouméa and Suva are also home to a number of key Pacific intergovernmental and development organisations, with the route providing another travel option for professionals, delegates, consultants and development partners travelling across the region.

Scurrah says passengers can connect through Nadi to destinations including Los Angeles, San Francisco, Vancouver, Honolulu, Sydney, Auckland, Singapore and Hong Kong.

The twice-weekly service starts today and will be operated using Fiji Link's ATR 72-600 aircraft.
